title: Merge In Between Linked Lists
statement:
You are given two singly linked lists, `list1` with `n` nodes and `list2` with `m` nodes, plus two positions `a` and `b` in `list1` (counted from 0 at its head). Cut the nodes at positions `a` through `b` (both included) out of `list1` and splice the whole of `list2` into the gap: the node at position `a - 1` must now lead to the head of `list2`, and the last node of `list2` must lead to the node that was at position `b + 1`. Return the head of the combined list. Because `1 <= a <= b < n - 1`, the first and last nodes of `list1` are never removed.

Each case is written as `[list1, a, b, list2]`, with both lists given as arrays of node values. Your function receives the head nodes of the two lists and the two integers; the list you return is shown as its array of values.
signature: ListNode mergeInBetween(ListNode list1, int a, int b, ListNode list2)
notes:
## Intuition

The simple route copies every value into an array, splices the arrays, and builds a fresh list. Linked lists make that unnecessary: after removing a stretch of `list1` and inserting `list2`, only two links differ from before. The node just before the cut must point to the head of `list2`, and the tail of `list2` must point to the node just after the cut. So the work is finding three nodes: the one at position `a - 1`, the one at position `b + 1`, and the last node of `list2`.

## Approach

1. Walk `a - 1` steps from the head of `list1` to reach `before`, the node at position `a - 1`.
2. From `before`, walk `b - a + 2` more steps to reach `after`, the node at position `b + 1`. Do this before changing any link.
3. Walk `tail` from the head of `list2` to its last node.
4. Point `before.next` at `list2` and `tail.next` at `after`.
5. The head of `list1` was not removed (since `a >= 1`), so return `list1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`list1 = 10 → 1 → 13 → 6 → 9 → 5`, `a = 3`, `b = 4`, `list2 = 1000000 → 1000001 → 1000002`.

- `before` takes 2 steps: 10, 1, 13. It stops at 13 (position 2).
- `after` starts at 13 and takes 3 steps: 6, 9, 5. It stops at 5 (position 5).
- `tail` walks `list2` to 1000002.
- Relink: `13 → 1000000` and `1000002 → 5`, giving `[10, 1, 13, 1000000, 1000001, 1000002, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(b + m): `list1` is walked only up to position `b + 1`, and `list2` once to its end.
- Space: O(1): three pointers; the existing nodes are reused.

## Pitfalls

- `before` must stop at position `a - 1`, one node earlier than the first removed node; stopping at `a` keeps a node that should be deleted.
- Find `after` before setting `before.next = list2`; once that link changes, walking on from `before` leads into `list2`.
- Positions count from 0, so `a = 3` removes the fourth node.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `before` | node of `list1` at position `a - 1`, the last one kept before the cut |
| `after` | node of `list1` at position `b + 1`, the first one kept after the cut |
| `tail` | last node of `list2` |
| `i` | position counter while walking `list1` |

narration.2: Start at the head of list1 to look for the node just before the cut.
narration.3: Take a - 1 steps so that before lands on position a - 1.
narration.6: The node after the cut lies further along, so continue from before.
narration.7: Steps from position a - 1 up to position b + 1: b - a + 2 of them.
narration.8: Move one node forward; at the end this is the first node kept after the cut.
narration.10: Now find the last node of list2.
narration.11: Keep going while there is another node after tail.
narration.14: Hook the head of list2 onto the node just before the cut; the removed nodes are skipped.
narration.15: Hook the rest of list1 onto the tail of list2.
narration.16: The head of list1 is never removed, so it is still the head of the answer.
